messages.content: "296 :     public boolean isUnixSymlink() {\n297 :         return (getUnixMode() & UnixStat.LINK_FLAG) == UnixStat.LINK_FLAG;\n298 :     }"

Title: Diagnosis

Details: The test is failing because the method isUnixSymlink() returns true when more than one flag is set in the Unix permissions, which should not be the case. Analyzing the code, isUnixSymlink() returns true if the bitwise AND between getUnixMode() and UnixStat.LINK_FLAG equals UnixStat.LINK_FLAG. The UnixStat.LINK_FLAG corresponds to the octal 0120000, which presumably indicates the symlink flag.

The getUnixMode() function returns 0 for non-Unix platforms. For Unix platforms, it extracts 16 bits of the external attributes shifted right by a constant SHORT_SHIFT and masked with SHORT_MASK.

The issue arises because the current check in isUnixSymlink() only verifies if the symlink bit is set but does not verify if it is the *only* permission bit set. If the Unix mode contains multiple flags, including the symlink flag, the method wrongly returns true, which is the problem described in the bug report and the failing test.

Hence, the root cause is that isUnixSymlink() does not ensure that the symlink flag is the only flag set in the file mode, leading to false positives for entries with multiple permission flags, such as mode 177777 in the bug report.

No other recent bug reports indicate a similar root cause, so we focus on this logic.

The fix should involve adjusting isUnixSymlink() or its usage to confirm that only the symlink flag is set, not just the presence of the symlink bit alone. 

This diagnosis matches the symptoms described in the issue report and explains why the test "isUnixSymlinkIsFalseIfMoreThanOneFlagIsSet" fails with entries whose Unix mode flags contain multiple bits including the symlink bit.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
